Asymptotic Covariance Matrix of the Sample Covariance Matrix Under Normality

Source: R/gammaN-gamma-mvn.R
GammaN.Rd

Returns the asymptotic covariance matrix \(\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{N}\) of the half-vectorization of the sample covariance matrix of x, assuming multivariate normality, $$ \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{N} = 2 \boldsymbol{D}_{k}^{+} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \otimes \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right) \boldsymbol{D}_{k}^{+ \prime}, $$ where \(\boldsymbol{D}_{k}^{+}\) is the Moore-Penrose inverse of the duplication matrix and \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\) is the sample covariance matrix of x, multiplied by \(n / (n - 1)\) when consistent = TRUE.

Usage

GammaN(x, consistent = TRUE)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector, matrix, or data frame. Data, with observations in rows.

consistent

Logical. If TRUE, multiply the sample covariance matrix by \(n / (n - 1)\).

Value

Returns a \(q \times q\) matrix, where \(q = k (k + 1) / 2\) and \(k\) is the number of variables.

Details

The function returns the output of the internal .GammaN() with sigmacap the (optionally rescaled) sample covariance matrix and pinv_of_dcap the Moore-Penrose inverse of the \(k \times k\) duplication matrix.

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

GammaN(x = datasets::mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt")])
#>            [,1]       [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,] 2811.87725 -396.08657  55.793534
#> [2,] -396.08657   64.95249 -10.439486
#> [3,]   55.79353  -10.43949   1.953324
